 Christian Braun 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Christian Braun accounted for 15 points (6-of-13 FGs), four assists, three steals, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Pelicans.
 Braun’s 15 points matched his season high, and just as important for fantasy managers were the other categories. He didn’t grab any rebounds, but the assists and steals should benefit category-league managers. Braun’s coming off a disappointing 2025-26, and the Nuggets need him to bounce back if they’re to be a true contender in the West. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Christian Braun 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #0

 Christian Braun amassed seven points (3-of-10 FGs), six rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer in Thursday’s loss to the Thunder. 
 While injuries played a role last season, Braun’s scoring average dropped by more than three points compared to his 2024-25 output. Unfortunately, the Nuggets guard got off to a slow start on Thursday, shooting 3-of-10 from the field. Braun was active on the glass, but the overall production was disappointing. 
 Christian Braun 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Christian Braun tallied 16 points (5-of-10 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, two steals and two three-pointers in Friday’s exhibition against the Lakers. 
 Braun finished his preseason with a solid performance on Friday, shooting 50 percent from the field and recording a solid stat line. Like Cameron Johnson, he’s looking to rebound from a disappointing 2025-26 season. With the talent Braun is surrounded by in Denver, he’ll have every opportunity to do so as a finisher playing off of Nikola Jokić and Jamal Murray. 
 Aaron Gordon 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #32 
 NBA insider Marc Stein reports that teams have registered interest in trading for Nuggets forward Aaron Gordon. 
 Despite being limited to 87 regular-season games over the last two seasons due to injuries. Gordon is a popular player heading into the offseason. According to Stein, the athletic forward is the veteran Nuggets player who has drawn the most trade interest from opposing teams. However, he also reported that if Denver were to make a move, they would prefer to find a trade partner for Christian Braun rather than for Gordon or Jamal Murray. Making a move would likely make it easier for the Nuggets to hold onto Peyton Watson, who will be a restricted free agent at the end of the month. 
 Christian Braun 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Christian Braun accounted for 18 points (5-of-9 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Monday’s Game 2 loss to the Timberwolves. 
 After scoring 12 points in Denver’s Game 1 victory on Saturday, Braun was more productive in Game 2. However, one of the main talking points from Monday’s defeat will be his missed free throw with the Nuggets trailing by two with 19 seconds remaining. Braun would hit the second to pull Denver to within one, but having to foul allowed Minnesota to extend his lead to three. Also, he’s one of the players the Nuggets will need to step up defensively, as they struggled on that end of the floor for most of the regular season and for parts of Game 2. 
 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Jamal Murray (shoulder), Christian Braun (ankle, hip) and Cameron Johnson (ankle) are out for Sunday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Murray, Braun and Johnson will remain out for Sunday’s regular-season finale. Tyus Jones, Bruce Brown and Julian Strawther started Friday’s win over the Thunder, and all should get another start on Sunday. For those in active leagues who need scoring, Strawther may be the best option to slot into fantasy lineups. 
 Christian Braun 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Christian Braun (ankle, hip) has been ruled out against the Thunder on Friday. 
 Braun will join the rest of the Denver starters as out for this game. Bruce Brown and Julian Strawther should both have a chance to start and take on extra minutes for the shorthanded Nuggets. 
 Christian Braun 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Christian Braun (ankle, hip) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Thunder. 
 With the Thunder sitting out most of their players, the Nuggets could follow suit on Friday. Denver still has work to do to lock up the No. 3 seed in the West, however, as they lead the Lakers by one game. If Braun doesn’t play, Bruce Brown would take on a more prominent role, possibly as a starter. 
 Christian Braun 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Christan Braun tallied 21 points (7-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Spurs. 
 Braun’s points tally has increased in each of his last four games. Saturday’s effort was his first of 20 points or more since March 18, when the Nuggets’ guard dropped 26 in a loss to the Grizzlies. Braun did more than score against the Spurs, recording a complete stat line in 39 minutes of play. These are the kind of all-around performances that Denver will need from Braun moving forward, even if he doesn’t surpass 20 points consistently. 
 Christian Braun 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Christian Braun added 18 points (7-of-11 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), six rebounds, four assists and one three-pointer in the win over the Jazz on Wednesday. 
 Like many other Nuggets starters, Braun had a productive evening against the Jazz. He logged 31 minutes and shot the ball efficiently, produced on the glass, and also made contributions as a passer. While Wednesday’s final line wasn’t a significant one, Braun was able to land his second consecutive double-digit scoring performance. His streak could extend to three games on Saturday against the Spurs. 
 Christian Braun 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Christian Braun finished Wednesday’s loss to the Grizzlies with 26 points (11-of-19 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, four steals and two three-pointers. 
 Braun logged his highest scoring performance of the season on Wednesday, finishing with 10 or more made field goals for the first time. His scoring came mostly from inside the arc, although a couple of made three-pointers helped him reach his new season-high. Yet, the versatile wing did more than just score; he was one of Denver’s top rebounders against Memphis, produced one of his highest assist totals, and also set a new season-high in steals. Braun’s balanced production was not rewarded with a win. However, his production may help some fantasy managers during the fantasy playoffs.

 This game had the outline of a monster fantasy performance with the rebounds and assists. Unfortunately he shot 4-17 from the field which puts a dampener on everything else.  Devin Vassell with 21 points (8-of-18 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, three steals and a three against the Jazz. 
 Vassell made some big shots in the fourth quarter to keep the Spurs in this game. While it was a good performance, he’s only up to 12.6 points, 4 rebounds, and 3.8 assists on the season. He’s a points and 3-point streamer who will occasionally have good games but is not a must in most redraft leagues. There’s too many high usage players on the team for him to be able to score like this consistently.

 Victor Wembanyama had 36 points (14-of-25 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 14 rebounds, five assists, two steals, two blocks and four 3-pointers in the 117-111 overtime win against the Jazz. 
 Wembanyama took advantage of the mediocre Jazz defense and got whatever he wanted in this game. His defensive presence changes how offenses attack the rim. He has been exactly what you wanted if you drafted him with the first pick in redraft leagues. Its hard to complain and you hope he doesn’t get hurt if you have him.

 Jalen Smith finished Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks with 17 points (7-of-12 FGs), 11 rebounds, five assists, three blocks and three three-pointers.
 While the Bulls await Nic Claxton’s return from a strained hamstring, Smith continues to provide reliable fantasy value. He finished Wednesday’s loss with his second double-double of the season and provided solid value in assists, blocks, and three-pointers. Smith is rostered in 46 percent of Yahoo leagues; managers needing a center for Friday’s 10-game slate should make sure he isn’t sitting on the waiver wire.

 Brice Sensabaugh is a bench scorer who thrives on hitting tough shots. While Lauri and Jaren are out, Brice could be looked at as a stream option if you need some points and three pointers, but he won’t give you much more than that.

 Caleb Wilson accounted for 20 points (7-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, two steals, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks.
 Wilson has scored 20 or more points in three of his last four games and continues to improve. The Bulls’ rookie didn’t shoot as well as he can against the Knicks, but he still made an impact on both ends of the floor. The Bulls led by as much as 19 in the third quarter before the Knicks rallied to win. Wilson will be a fun player to watch develop in the years to come, and his fantasy value should only improve.

 Darryn Peterson put up 18 points (4-of-13 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, a steal, and three 3-pointers in an overtime loss to the Spurs. 
 Obviously you want Darryn to be more efficient from the field, but he got his shot attempts up which is what you want to see. He did leave the game in the first quarter with a head injury but returned. He did not close the game which is notable. He will continue to get better, and this is a good game all things considered, but the fantasy upside for this season isn’t very high.

 Matas Buzelis accumulated 17 points (5-of-13 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks.
 Buzelis is shooting just 38.8 percent from the field this season, seven percentage points lower than his career number. He was 2-of-7 inside the arc on Wednesday, but the Bulls forward made half of his six three-point attempts. Add in the full stat line, and things could have gone far worse for those rostering Buzelis.

 Norman Powell produced 30 points (10-of-15 FGs, 6-of-9 FTs), two rebounds, two assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks.
 Powell finished Wednesday’s defeat with his first 30-point game of the season, shooting 66.7 percent from the field. The veteran guard began the day shooting 36.5 percent from the field, so category-league managers will be pleased with Powell’s showing against the Knicks. Things won’t get easier for Powell and the Bulls, as they visit the Celtics on Friday. Boston blew out Chicago on Friday, with Powell scoring 20 points.

 Ace Bailey had 19 points (9-of-18 FGs), six rebounds, a block and a three in 39 minutes and 30 seconds of play against the Spurs. 
 Ace Bailey is the best point of attack defender the Jazz have on the roster right now. He’s also put in serious work on the offseason to get better at rebounding the ball and passing. The amount of trust the coaching staff has in him right now cannot be understated. He’s worth grabbing in redraft leagues if he’s available, and in dynasty leagues, you have to be happy if you have him on your roster.
